title: Cystic Pancreatic Neoplasms and Annular Pancreas

steps.tx: With the widespread utilization of cross-sectional abdominal imaging, primary **pancreatic cystic neoplasms** are increasingly identified as incidental findings in asymptomatic individuals. These true neoplasms are lined by an epithelial layer and are broadly divided into serous cystadenomas, mucinous cystic neoplasms, intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms, and solid pseudopapillary neoplasms. Accurate preoperative differentiation is crucial to distinguish benign entities from lesions possessing high malignant potential.
steps.say: Pancreatic cystic neoplasms are true epithelial-lined cysts that require differentiation between benign lesions and premalignant mucinous tumours.

vis.alt: Pathological diagram showing distinctive multilocular appearance of mucinous cystic neoplasm with ovarian-type stroma.
vis.caption: Mucinous cystic neoplasm: thick-walled multilocular lesion with characteristic ovarian-type stroma. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Accounting for thirty percent of cystic tumours, **serous cystadenoma** is a completely benign neoplasm that exhibits an overwhelming female preponderance. Microscopic examination demonstrates numerous tiny, microcystic spaces lined by glycogen-rich, cuboidal epithelium that stains strongly with periodic acid-Schiff. Cross-sectional imaging reveals a classic honeycomb or sponge-like cluster of microcysts with a pathognomonic central calcified stellate scar.
steps.say: Serous cystadenoma is a benign multilocular lesion of glycogen-rich cuboidal cells, showing a characteristic central stellate calcified scar.

steps.tx: In sharp contrast, a **mucinous cystic neoplasm** carries substantial premalignant potential, with invasive carcinoma present in ten to thirty percent of resected specimens. These thick-walled macrocystic tumours occur almost exclusively in middle-aged women and predominate in the pancreatic body and tail. The pathognomonic histopathological hallmark is the presence of subepithelial ovarian-type stroma expressing progesterone and estrogen receptors beneath mucin-secreting columnar cells.
steps.say: Mucinous cystic neoplasms occur in female patients in the pancreatic body or tail, featuring diagnostic ovarian-type stroma and malignant potential.

steps.tx: Another common mucin-producing neoplasm is intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm, which communicates directly with the pancreatic ductal system. Divided into main-duct, branch-duct, and mixed varieties, main-duct lesions carry an alarming malignant risk exceeding sixty percent, warranting prompt surgical resection. Conversely, asymptomatic branch-duct IPMNs lacking high-risk stigmata such as jaundice, enhancing mural nodules, or duct dilatation above ten millimetres can be monitored with serial **magnetic resonance imaging**.
steps.say: Intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasms communicate with pancreatic ducts, with main-duct lesions carrying high cancer risks warranting resection.

steps.tx: A unique embryological developmental malformation that encircles and compresses the second part of the duodenum is **annular pancreas**. This anomaly results from failure of the ventral pancreatic bud to complete its normal clockwise rotation behind the duodenum during the seventh week of gestation. Instead, the bifid ventral bud remains fixed anteriorly, stretching a ring of normal pancreatic tissue circumferentially around the descending duodenum.
steps.say: Annular pancreas develops from abnormal migration of the ventral pancreatic bud, forming a ring of pancreatic tissue encircling the duodenum.

vis.alt: Infant abdominal radiograph demonstrating double bubble sign of duodenal obstruction in neonatal annular pancreas.
vis.caption: Annular pancreas: neonatal duodenal obstruction with classic double bubble appearance on abdominal radiography. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: In neonates, annular pancreas presents with non-bilious or bilious vomiting shortly after birth depending on whether the duodenal ring encircles above or below the ampulla of Vater. Plain abdominal radiographs characteristically demonstrate the pathognomonic **double bubble sign**, representing gas distending the stomach and the dilated first part of the duodenum, with complete absence of gas throughout the distal gastrointestinal tract.
steps.say: Neonatal annular pancreas presents with vomiting and shows a double bubble sign on plain abdominal X-ray.

nodes.label: Failure of Ventral Pancreatic Bud Migration
Fibro-Glandular Ring Encircles Second Part of Duodenum
Erect Radiograph: Pathognomonic Double Bubble Sign

steps.tx: While acute duodenal obstruction manifests in neonates, nearly fifty percent of annular pancreas cases remain asymptomatic until adulthood. Adult patients typically present in their thirties to fifties with postprandial fullness, recurrent peptic ulcer disease, acute pancreatitis, or chronic gastric outlet obstruction. Upper gastrointestinal contrast studies and magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography establish the diagnosis by showing extrinsic concentric **duodenal narrowing** encircled by pancreatic ductal branches.
steps.say: Adult annular pancreas manifests as postprandial fullness, peptic ulceration, or recurrent pancreatitis secondary to chronic duodenal narrowing.

steps.tx: Surgical management of annular pancreas strictly forbids direct division or resection of the encircling pancreatic ring because it shares its blood supply with the duodenal wall and contains major tributary ducts. Division invariably provokes catastrophic pancreatic fistulas, acute pancreatitis, or duodenal necrosis. Instead, surgical relief is accomplished through bypass of the obstructed segment using a **duodenoduodenostomy** or side-to-side duodenojejunostomy.
steps.say: Direct division of the annular ring is avoided due to fistula hazards, requiring duodenoduodenostomy bypass to relieve obstruction.
